debrief.whyItWorks: When most positions are unknown and the clock is long, information converts the execute from a guess into a read. Here, 2 players faced 3 with about 78 seconds left.
debrief.cost: It spends round clock, which limits the later options.
debrief.assumption: There is enough clock left to act on whatever the information shows.
debrief.breaksWhen: The clock runs down before the information is used, so the team has to execute blind anyway.

evidenceReview.explanation: Unaccounted-for opponents are the main risk to any committed plan and the main reason to gather information. Here 2 defenders could not be placed.
The round clock bounds how long any plan can take. Here the round clock stood near 78 seconds.
The head count sets how many duels the team can lose and still carry out its plan. Here it was 2 against 3.

debrief.followupReview: The proposed best answer to the new information was: Adjust the plan to the new information. Reasoning: the new information shows where an opponent is or what utility they have used, so adapting the plan is worth more than repeating it.
debrief.strongestAlternative: The closest alternative was to commit to an execute now, spending utility and options at once for a plant before the clock runs low.

counterfactual.changedFact: The round clock is under half a minute.
counterfactual.effect: Gathering information no longer fits, and committing at once becomes stronger.

reveal.principle: Decide when to stop gathering information: keep reading while the clock is long and positions are unknown, and commit once the clock or the numbers force the plan.
